item.title: Rising payment costs push Uber to drop Visa in Kenya
item.description: Uber has stopped accepting Visa cards in Kenya, cutting off a payment option once central to its pitch to business travellers and expatriates in East Africa’s biggest ride-hailing market.

item.description: Silverbacks is now shifting its sights to African sports, a less-invested sector.

item.title: Pan-African fintech NALA deepens stablecoin rails to speed up dollar flows
item.description: Building on the March 2024 debut of its B2B payments platform, Rafiki, NALA is deepening its stablecoin payment rails, aiming to speed up dollar flows into emerging markets where SMEs face delays and high costs moving money. The new network, integrated into Rafiki, will allow global firms operating in Africa and Asia to collect funds in US dollars and pay out local currencies within minutes, using stablecoins as a settlement layer.

item.title: What 2025 revealed about Francophone Africa’s tech ecosystem ambitions
item.description: Francophone Africa, stretching from Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire in the west, through Cameroon and central Africa, to Morocco and Tunisia in the north, is experiencing strong but uneven startup growth. While the region still trails Anglophone hubs like Nairobi and Lagos in total capital raised, innovation (mainly in fintech) is deeply embedded, and non-fintech segments are finally attracting attention from builders and investors alike.

item.title: Amazon’s Kuiper satellite secures Nigerian permit to begin operations in 2026
item.description: Project Kuiper, the Amazon-owned ​​satellite internet initiative, has secured a landing permit from the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to begin operations from 2026.

item.title: Uganda orders nationwide internet shutdown ahead of polls
item.description: In a letter dated January 13 seen by TechCabal, Uganda Communications Commission (UCC) said the measures would take effect from 6:00 pm local time on Tuesday and would remain in place until further notice.
